prompts.display_text: Pin a country where a new temple was announced at the October 2021 general conference.
prompts.text_original: Pin a country where a new temple was announced at the October 2021 general conference.
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org temple milestones, read 27 Oct 2026; Church Newsroom conference temple announcement
prompts.summary: At the end of the October 2021 general conference, President Russell M. Nelson announced 13 new temples in 10 countries or territories. Antananarivo and Monrovia were the first temples announced for Madagascar and Liberia.

answers.name: United States of America
answers.fact: Cody Wyoming; Fort Worth Texas; Heber Valley Utah; and 1 more.

answers.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
answers.fact: Kananga Democratic Republic of the Congo.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country whose second dedicated temple was dedicated in 2010 or later.
prompts.text_original: Pin a country whose second dedicated temple was dedicated in 2010 or later.
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronology and milestones, read 27 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: A country's second temple usually means the Church there has grown past what one temple can serve. Each answer names the country's second temple to be dedicated and its date, counting only temples now in operation.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory in Mexico, Central America or the Caribbean where a current Seventy served as a young missionary.
prompts.text_original: Several General Authority Seventies serving as of October 2026 were once young full-time missionaries in Mexico, Central America or the Caribbean. Pin a country or territory there where one of them served, as named in the Church's official biographies.
prompts.citation: Church leader biographies, General Authority Seventies, read 27 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: As of October 2026, the biographies of current General Authority Seventies name young missions in Mexico, Guatemala, El Salvador, the Dominican Republic, Puerto Rico and Jamaica. Elder Kevin G. Brown served in his native Jamaica.

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: Mexico Hermosillo, Monterrey, Torreon, Tampico and North missions, and Veracruz.

answers.name: Dominican Republic
answers.fact: Dominican Republic Santo Domingo East Mission (Elder Eddy).

answers.name: El Salvador
answers.fact: El Salvador missions (Elders Nash and Cordon).

answers.name: Puerto Rico
answers.fact: Puerto Rico San Juan Mission (Elder Corbitt).

answers.name: Jamaica
answers.fact: Jamaica Kingston Mission (Elder Kevin G. Brown).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country that Church Global Histories say was dedicated for preaching the gospel in 1850-1881
prompts.text_original: A country that, per its Church Global Histories chronology, an apostle or missionary formally dedicated for the preaching of the gospel between 1850 and 1881.
prompts.citation: Church Global Histories chronologies: France, Italy, Switzerland, South Africa, Sweden, Mexico
prompts.note: Israel does not count: the 1873 Mount of Olives prayer was for the gathering of the Jews, not a dedication for preaching.
prompts.summary: Opening a new land often began with a prayer of dedication. Global Histories record John Taylor dedicating France and Lorenzo Snow dedicating Italy in 1850, Snow dedicating Switzerland in 1851, missionaries on Lion's Head above Cape Town in 1853, Sweden in 1857 and Moses Thatcher in Mexico in 1880-81.

answers.name: France
answers.fact: 1850: John Taylor dedicated France for missionary work.

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: 1850: Lorenzo Snow, T. B. H. Stenhouse and Jabez Woodard dedicated Italy.

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: 1880-81: Moses Thatcher dedicated Mexico for missionary work.

answers.name: Sweden
answers.fact: 1857: Apostle Ezra T. Benson and mission leaders dedicated Sweden for preaching.

answers.name: South Africa
answers.fact: 1853: missionaries dedicated the land on Lion's Head above Cape Town.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country outside the United States that Gordon B. Hinckley visited in 1998
prompts.text_original: In 1998 President Gordon B. Hinckley traveled about 77,000 miles to meet Saints around the world. A country outside the United States that he visited that year.
prompts.summary: Gordon B. Hinckley logged about 77,000 miles in 1998. In February he toured West, East and Southern Africa, announcing a temple in Accra and stopping in Cape Verde and the Canary Islands. He also visited northern Mexico, western Europe including Preston, England, nine Canadian cities, and in November Nicaragua and Honduras.

answers.name: Canada
answers.fact: An August tour of nine Canadian cities, including Halifax.

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: In March he visited 10 cities in northern Mexico.

answers.name: Switzerland
answers.fact: Geneva, on the June European trip.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: Frankfurt, on the June European trip.

answers.name: Ghana
answers.fact: In Accra on February 16 he announced a temple for Ghana.

answers.name: South Africa
answers.fact: Johannesburg, Durban and Cape Town, February.

answers.name: Spain
answers.fact: Las Palmas in the Canary Islands, February 13.

answers.name: Honduras
answers.fact: San Pedro Sula and Tegucigalpa, November.
